title: Doc Cook, drinking, and sporting-house pianists such as Jimmy Johnson
summary: Punch talks about drinking, says early New Orleans bands used no piano, and recalls pianists like the Todds and a Jimmy Johnson.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Yeah. But Doc Cook played in the same place and I worked with him at the Dream Land. Well you know Keppert played with Cook and you played with Cook too. Yeah. Is that the same place? But I thought that was Fred's band. I didn't know no band. No, I didn't know. It was Cook's. Yes it was. Old Freddy Keppert was a fine fella boy. Drank pretty good didn't he? Oh he could drink some liquor. Did you drink very much when you was younger? Yeah I did a lot of drinking. Did you? Yeah but I tell you what happened with me. When I got to Chicago among all them kind of people I laid off liquor for a long time. You did? Yeah I got straight there but then they come to find that I was less of you too. But I stayed with him over two years. Yeah. Do you recall during these early days here in New Orleans some of the piano players that you knew? Well now I'm going to be straight Rich. In New Orleans back then in them early times we didn't never use a piano. You didn't? No sir. Never did. What did you use? Clannet, guitar, banjo, bass, violin, trumpet and drums. Yeah but all these whorehouses had pianos. Well the piano was by themselves mostly. They were? Yes sir. They never played with the group? No sir. Alright now would they have, would they have? I know there are plenty of piano players in them whorehouses. Who were some of them? Clowns, Todd. They had a sister named Camille Todd played in the sporting house. Clarence Todd and Camilla Todd and who else? And uh, Jimmy, Jimmy, Jimmy, Jimmy Jimson or Jimmy Johnson or something. Jimmy Johnson? Yeah. James P? P John, but he had the band but he had a piano player there see. Well James P was a piano player. Well him, that's who he was. I didn't know. I didn't know.
Was this the guy from New York City? Yeah I think he was. Did you know him later in New York? I don't know.
